newsitem.title: UK: United News down after HTV offer.
newsitem.headline: United News down after HTV offer.

text.p: Shares in United News & Media Plc dropped on Friday after the broadcasting-to-financial services group announced an agreed 372 million stg bid for HTV Group Plc.
From being up 2p before the bid was announced, United News shares were down 10p at 714 by 1419 GMT. HTV shares were up 84-1/2p at 415, just under the level of United's 420p-per-share cash bid.
Dealers and analysts said the deal was not a major surprise and though the price at first sight looked a little high, there was no obvious big negative in the deal for United News shares.
However they added that a more considered reaction would probably not come until after an analyst meeting due to start at 1500 GMT.
"It is a slightly higher multiple than Granada's acquisition of YTV," said one analyst, "but there is a consolidation going on in the industry and they are paying the price they have to pay."
United, which already held a near 30 percent stake in HTV, said the takeover would have a neutral impact on its earnings in the first year.
